summary: Ikuro Hattori holds a Ph.D. from the University of Pune and works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Affiliations include the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2003, 2026) and Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2026).

Ildikó Puskás (1942–2009) was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied under János Harmatta from around 1963 to 1968 and held a position at Eötvös Loránd University from circa 1970 until 2009.

Ilkka Pyysiäinen (born 1959) is a religious studies scholar who studied under René Gothóni around 1988–1993. He served as an Academy Research Fellow at the University of Helsinki in 1984 and as a visiting researcher at the University of Oxford.

Ilya Gershevitch (1914–2001) worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistic studies. He studied under Antonino Pagliaro, Walter Bruno Henning, and Harold Walter Bailey, and held posts at the University of Cambridge (1948–1965), Jesus College (1962), and Columbia University (1960–1961).

Immanuel Bekker (1785–1871) was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (circa 1803–1807), taught Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler, and held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1810 to 1871.

Imran Philip specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed doctoral studies under the supervision of Kaustubh Mani Sengupta (attested 2026) and held a Dr. Zakir Hussain Fellowship at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Imre Bangha (born 1967) works in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Visva-Bharati University (PhD 1998), later holding positions at Visva-Bharati, the University of Oxford and Wolfson College (circa 2003), and Eötvös Loránd University (attested 2026).

Imre Galambos (born 1967) works in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. Educated at ELTE, Nankai University, and UC Berkeley (PhD), he held posts at UC Santa Barbara, the British Library, Cambridge, Hamburg, and Zhejiang University.

Imre Hamar (born 1967) studied at Eötvös Loránd University, National Taiwan Normal University, and under advisor Noritoshi Aramaki (~1995–1997). He became a professor at Eötvös Loránd University in 2006 and has served as a visiting professor at Otani University.

Imtiyaz Yusuf works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. from Temple University (1984–1990) and was appointed professor at the International Islamic University Malaysia in 2019.

In-gun Kang is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Heythrop College under Michael Barnes, at the Jesuit School of Theology of Santa Clara University, and at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under several teachers.

Indira Viswanathan Peterson (born 1950) is an Indologist who studied at the University of Mumbai and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. She held posts at Columbia University (~1980–1983) and Mount Holyoke College (~1983–2019).

Ines Konczak-Nagel specializes in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She held posts at the Saxon Academy, Berlin State Museums, Ryukoku University (2012), and the University of Leipzig (attested 2026).

Ingmar Heise works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned an MA in Chinese Studies from Leiden University (completed by 2005) and pursued doctoral studies at the University of Bristol (attested 2012).

Ingo Strauch works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the Free University of Berlin (-2000), where he was attested in 2008, and was appointed professor at the University of Lausanne in 2012.
Inyoung Chung is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Virginia under the doctoral supervision of Paul Groner (attested 2008).

Ioan Mihălcescu (1874–1948) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Bucharest, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the University of Leipzig (Ph.D. 1901–1904), later serving as a Privatdozent at Bucharest in 1904.

Ioan Petru Culianu (1950–1991) worked in religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Bucharest, Sacro Cuore, and Paris-Sorbonne, mentored by Mircea Eliade. He held academic posts at the University of Groningen (1976–1986) and the University of Chicago (1986–1991).
Iona Macgregor is an Indology and linguistics scholar affiliated with the University of Hamburg as a project staff member (attested 2026).
Ippei Okamoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Okamoto held posts at Toyo University (attested 2014) and Minobusan University (attested 2026).
